test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 6 days. B alone can do the same work in 7 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio (A+B) : B = (1/6) : (1/7) = 7 : 6

Efficiency of A = (Efficiency of A+B) − (Efficiency of B) = 7 − 6 = 1 unit

Total Work = LCM(6, 7) = 42 units

Double the work = 42 × 2 = 84 units

Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 1 = 84 days

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 6 days

Time taken by B alone = 7 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total work be LCM of 6 and 7 = 42 units.

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of A = (Efficiency of A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 7 − 6 = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Double the work = 2 × 42 = 84 units.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete double work = 84 ÷ 1 = 84 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total work is always assumed to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual time taken by different persons to simplify efficiency calculations.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to time and work, where an inlet pipe has positive efficiency and an outlet/leakage pipe has negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals, which is often the same as the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.
